case.summary: Analyst flagged a suspicious device profile (SM-G935F, Android 7.0) used across multiple cards this month. Graph traversal revealed the same device, always behind an anonymous proxy and marked New, was used to make 1–3 mid-sized purchases on 44 cards (24 in Aug–Sep 2016; 20 since 11 November 2016), then abandoned—a coordinated pattern matching none of the known fraud categories. Customer C13487 denied both unauthorized transactions on card C13487-K1 ($112.37 on 15 November, $74.96 on 22 November), confirming fraud at probability 0.9. Card blocked; case created and escalated to analyst; Suspicious Activity Report filed; 19 other cards sharing the device are now under monitoring per Policies R2, R6, and R9.

sar.narrative: Customer C13487, card C13487-K1, reports unauthorized online purchases on 15 November 2016 ($112.37) and 22 November 2016 ($74.96) and states the card remains in their possession. Both transactions originated from device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080 operating behind an anonymous IP proxy, marked New to this account. Bank investigation identified the same device profile and proxy in use across 44 customer cards over two months (24 cards in August–September 2016; 20 cards from 14 November 2016 onward), with each card showing 1–3 online purchases of $35–$250 followed by no further activity from that device—a coordinated pattern inconsistent with legitimate use. The device appears in four previously confirmed fraud cases (CC-2971, CC-3035, CC-2649, CC-2985). Cardholder confirmed denial; fraud probability assessed at 0.9. Actions taken: card C13487-K1 blocked; case HHG-014 created for investigation and escalated to analyst; 19 connected cards placed under monitoring; graph evidence retained to support ongoing analysis of the shared device profile (Policy R6, R9).
